mainText: Good morning, Landon. Here's your brief for Friday, November 20, 2026. Let's start with the markets. Stocks fell sharply on Thursday. The S&P 500 dropped 2 percent to 7,175, its sixth straight losing session. The Dow lost about 1,100 points, or 2.2 percent, to 49,097. The Nasdaq fell 2.3 percent to 23,879. The main driver was another selloff in artificial intelligence stocks, with Nvidia down more than 3 percent and Broadcom down about 2 percent, as worries grew that the AI boom may be cooling. On the Fed, markets now see a December rate hike as close to certain. CME FedWatch data put the odds of an increase at the December 9 meeting at roughly 95 percent, with most of that on a quarter point move. The target range currently sits at 3.75 to 4 percent. Governor Christopher Waller has said he supports a larger half point hike, pointing to core inflation running around 3.5 percent on a three month annualized basis. New York Fed President John Williams pushed back, saying the situation does not call for dramatic action. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem has said he sees several hikes ahead before next spring. Next, Anthropic made its stock market debut. The AI company priced its initial public offering at 83 dollars a share, above its expected range, and sold about 980 million shares. The stock opened roughly 34 percent higher and closed its first day at about 97 dollars, up a little more than 17 percent. Next, Walmart reported third quarter revenue of 188.8 billion dollars, up 5.2 percent, and raised its full year sales and profit outlook. Even so, the stock slipped about 1 percent, as U.S. same store sales growth of 2.9 percent came in a bit below expectations. Next, Intuit beat estimates after the bell, with adjusted earnings of 2 dollars and 91 cents a share on revenue of 4.35 billion dollars, up 12 percent. But its full year guidance only roughly matched Wall Street forecasts, and shares fell about 13 percent in after hours trading. And finally, Ross Stores posted strong third quarter results, with comparable store sales up 8 percent and earnings of 1 dollar and 91 cents a share, up from 1 dollar and 58 cents a year ago. Shares still dipped in late trading. On the calendar today, BJ's Wholesale reports before the open. The University of Michigan releases its final November consumer sentiment reading, including inflation expectations, at 8 a.m. Mountain time. Fed Governors Waller and Lisa Cook are both scheduled to speak. Here's your fun fact. Greenland sharks, which may live for several centuries, often have parasitic crustaceans clamped onto their eyes that feed on the cornea, so scientists long assumed the sharks were essentially blind. But a study published this year found their retinas remain fully equipped for vision, even in a shark estimated to be about 130 years old. Researchers think strong DNA repair genes may help keep their eyes working for centuries. Have a great day.
